questions.question: In a network of stations $1,\ldots,M$ with Markov routing and routing matrix $\boldsymbol{P}=(P_{ij})$, what does the entry $P_{ij}$ (row $i$, column $j$) give?
options: The probability that a job arriving at station $i$ has just come from station $j$.
The probability that a job finishing service at station $i$ goes next to station $j$.
The probability that a job served at station $i$ visits station $j$ at some later time.
The probability that a job entering the network at station $i$ leaves it from station $j$.

questions.question: Under Markov routing in a network of stations $1,\ldots,M$, a job finishing service moves next to station $j$ with a probability given by the routing matrix $\boldsymbol{P}$. Which of the following is this probability allowed to depend on?
options: The number of jobs currently waiting at the destination station $j$.
The number of times the job has already visited the station it is leaving.
The length of the service the job has just completed.
The station $i$ at which the job has just finished service.

questions.question: For a network of stations $1,\ldots,M$ with Markov routing, which property holds for every routing matrix $\boldsymbol{P}=(P_{ij})$?
options: All entries are non-negative and every row sums to at most $1$.
All entries are non-negative and every column sums to at most $1$.
All entries are non-negative and every row sums to exactly $1$.
All entries are non-negative and every diagonal entry equals $0$.

questions.question: In a network of stations $1,\ldots,M$ with routing matrix $\boldsymbol{P}$, the exit probability of station $1$ is $P_{10}=1-\sum_{j=1}^{M}P_{1j}=0$. What does this mean?
options: No job ever leaves the network, at whichever of the stations it has been served.
Every job served at station $1$ moves on to a station of the network, possibly station $1$.
No external jobs arrive at station $1$, so all its jobs come from other stations.
All entries in row $1$ of $\boldsymbol{P}$ are zero, so station $1$ sends no jobs anywhere.

questions.question: A three-station network has routing matrix $\boldsymbol{P}=\begin{pmatrix}0&0.5&0.35\\0.25&0.15&0.4\\0.1&0.05&0\end{pmatrix}$. What is the exit probability $P_{20}$, the probability that a job leaves the network after service at station $2$?

In a two-station network, $70\%$ of the jobs finishing service at station $1$ go to station $2$ and the other $30\%$ leave; $40\%$ of the jobs finishing at station $2$ return to station $1$ and the rest leave. Which matrix is the routing matrix $\boldsymbol{P}$?
options: $\begin{pmatrix}0&0.7\\0.4&0\end{pmatrix}$
$\begin{pmatrix}0&0.4\\0.7&0\end{pmatrix}$
$\begin{pmatrix}0.3&0.7\\0.4&0.6\end{pmatrix}$
$\begin{pmatrix}0&0.7\\0.6&0\end{pmatrix}$

questions.question: In a stable network with Markov routing, station $1$ has total arrival rate (and hence departure rate) $\lambda_1=5$ jobs per hour, and its routing probability to station $3$ is $P_{13}=0.4$. At what rate do jobs move from station $1$ to station $3$?
options: $3$ jobs per hour
$12.5$ jobs per hour
$0.4$ jobs per hour
$2$ jobs per hour

questions.question: Which matrix is a valid routing matrix $\boldsymbol{P}$ for an open two-station network with external arrivals, in which jobs can leave?
options: $\begin{pmatrix}0.5&0.6\\0.2&0.3\end{pmatrix}$
$\begin{pmatrix}0.1&0.8\\0.3&0.6\end{pmatrix}$
$\begin{pmatrix}0.6&0.4\\0.3&0.7\end{pmatrix}$
$\begin{pmatrix}1.2&-0.4\\0.1&0.5\end{pmatrix}$

questions.question: In a network of stations $1,\ldots,M$ with routing matrix $\boldsymbol{P}$ and total arrival rates $\lambda_1,\ldots,\lambda_M$, which expression gives the rate at which jobs that have just been served at some station of the network (possibly $j$ itself) arrive at station $j$?
options: $\lambda_j\sum_{i=1}^{M}P_{ji}$
$\sum_{i=1}^{M}\lambda_iP_{ji}$
$\sum_{i=1}^{M}\lambda_jP_{ij}$
$\sum_{i=1}^{M}\lambda_iP_{ij}$

questions.question: In a stable network with Markov routing, station $i$ has departure rate $\lambda_i$ and routing probability $P_{ij}$ to station $j$. Under which condition do the jobs sent from station $i$ to station $j$ form a stream of rate $\lambda_iP_{ij}$?
options: Under no extra condition: each departure goes to $j$ with probability $P_{ij}$, whatever the service times.
Only if service times at station $i$ are exponential, so that departures from $i$ are Poisson.
Only if $P_{ii}=0$, because jobs fed back to station $i$ would be counted twice in $\lambda_i$.
Only if the external arrivals at station $i$ form a Poisson process, since thinning needs a Poisson input.

questions.question: In a stable open network with routing matrix $\boldsymbol{P}$, external arrival rates $\gamma_1,\ldots,\gamma_M$ with $|\boldsymbol{\gamma}|=\sum_i\gamma_i>0$, and total arrival rates $\lambda_i$ solving the traffic equations, what does the ratio $\lambda_i/|\boldsymbol{\gamma}|$ measure?
options: The probability that a job visits station $i$ at least once during its stay in the network.
The mean number of visits that a job makes to station $i$ during its stay in the network.
The fraction of time that station $i$ is busy serving jobs, in the long run.
The fraction of all station visits in the network that are made to station $i$.

questions.question: Jobs arrive from outside at a machine (station $1$) at rate $\gamma_1=4$ per hour, then go to an inspection station (station $2$), which sends $20\%$ back to the machine and lets the rest leave: $P_{12}=1$, $P_{21}=0.2$, $P_{20}=0.8$. What is the total arrival rate $\lambda_1$ at the machine?
options: $4.8$ per hour
$3.2$ per hour
$5$ per hour
$4$ per hour

questions.question: A stable open network has routing matrix $\boldsymbol{P}=\begin{pmatrix}0&0.6&0.4\\0&0&0.5\\0.5&0&0\end{pmatrix}$, and the total arrival rates are $\lambda_1=20$, $\lambda_2=12$, $\lambda_3=14$ jobs per hour. At what total rate do jobs leave the network?
options: $46$ jobs per hour
$33$ jobs per hour
$16.2$ jobs per hour
$13$ jobs per hour

questions.question: A network with Markov routing has routing matrix $\boldsymbol{P}=\begin{pmatrix}0.1&0.5&0.2\\0.3&0&0.6\\0&0.4&0.2\end{pmatrix}$. What is the probability that a job finishing service at station $1$ is routed to some station $k$ and, after its service at $k$, is routed to station $3$?

In a two-station network every job follows the same route: station $1$, then station $2$, then station $1$ again, and then it leaves. Can this route be described exactly by Markov routing with a routing matrix $\boldsymbol{P}$ on stations $1$ and $2$?
options: Yes: take $P_{12}=P_{10}=1/2$ and $P_{21}=1$, since half of the departures from station $1$ go to station $2$.
No: after station $1$ the next step depends on whether it is the first or the second visit.
Yes: take $P_{12}=1$ and $P_{21}=1$, since these are exactly the moves that every job makes.
Yes: take $P_{12}=1$, $P_{21}=1$ and $P_{10}=1$, listing every move that the route uses.

questions.question: An open network has routing matrix $\boldsymbol{P}$ and external arrival rates $\gamma_i$ with $\sum_i\gamma_i>0$. How does the condition 'at least one station has exit probability $P_{i0}>0$' relate to the traffic equations having a finite solution?
options: It is necessary and sufficient, because a single exit lets every job drain from the network.
It is sufficient but not necessary, because jobs can also leave through columns that sum to less than $1$.
It is necessary but not sufficient, because jobs must be able to reach a station with an exit.
It is not needed: with every row summing to $1$, the rates stay finite when the $\gamma_i$ are small.

questions.question: A two-station network has routing matrix $\boldsymbol{P}=\begin{pmatrix}0.5&0.3\\0&0\end{pmatrix}$, so $P_{10}=0.2$ and $P_{20}=1$. Which statement about the powers $\boldsymbol{P}^k$ and the jobs in this network is correct?
options: $\boldsymbol{P}^2=\boldsymbol{0}$, since with two stations every job has left after two routing steps.
$\boldsymbol{P}^k\ne\boldsymbol{0}$ for every $k$, so a positive fraction of jobs remains in the network for ever.
$\boldsymbol{P}^k=\boldsymbol{0}$ for some $k\ge3$, since every job eventually leaves the network.
$\boldsymbol{P}^k\ne\boldsymbol{0}$ for every $k$, yet every job leaves the network with probability $1$.

questions.question: Jobs arrive from outside only at station $1$, at rate $\gamma_1=1$, and the routing matrix is $\boldsymbol{P}=\begin{pmatrix}0.4&0.6\\\beta&0.2\end{pmatrix}$ with $0\le\beta\le0.8$. For which $\beta$ do the traffic equations $\lambda_j=\gamma_j+\sum_i\lambda_iP_{ij}$ have a finite solution?
options: Exactly for $\beta<0.8$.
For every $\beta$ with $0\le\beta\le0.8$.
For no $\beta$, because row $1$ sums to $1$ and station $1$ has no exit.
Exactly for $\beta<0.6$, so that column $1$ sums to $0.4+\beta<1$.
